classification.difficultyReason: Use kite or rhombus symmetry to recover a full diagonal from a half-diagonal, discard irrelevant side lengths, and then apply the appropriate area formula.

content.prompt: Calculate the area of these shapes.

spec.description: Right-pointing kite with a shorter left portion, dashed perpendicular diagonals and an external horizontal dimension.
spec.mathematics: Full horizontal diagonal 40 cm; upper vertical half-diagonal 13 cm. Both left sides have double equality ticks and both right sides have single equality ticks. A right-angle marker identifies the perpendicular diagonals.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; the full vertical diagonal and area belong in the answer.

answer.worked:
The horizontal diagonal bisects the vertical diagonal.
$$\begin{align*}y&=2\times13\\y&=26\text{ cm}\\A&=\frac{xy}{2}\\A&=\frac{40\times26}{2}\\A&=520\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Wide diamond-shaped rhombus with an external horizontal dimension above it and dashed perpendicular diagonals.
spec.mathematics: Full horizontal diagonal 17 mm; upper vertical half-diagonal 6 mm; lower-left side 10.4 mm. All four sides have matching single equality ticks. The side length is retained as a rounded, redundant given.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; the full vertical diagonal and area belong in the answer.

answer.worked:
The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other.
$$\begin{align*}y&=2\times6\\y&=12\text{ mm}\\A&=\frac{xy}{2}\\A&=\frac{17\times12}{2}\\A&=102\text{ mm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Upright kite with a short upper portion, longer lower portion and a vertical external dimension to the right.
spec.mathematics: Full vertical diagonal 3 cm; right horizontal half-diagonal 1.05 cm; upper-left side 1.38 cm; lower-right side 2.35 cm. Double ticks mark the upper pair and single ticks mark the lower pair. The vertical diagonal and only the right half of the horizontal diagonal are dashed. A right-angle marker is at their intersection.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; the full horizontal diagonal and area belong in the answer.

answer.worked:
The vertical diagonal bisects the horizontal diagonal.
$$\begin{align*}x&=2\times1.05\\x&=2.1\text{ cm}\\A&=\frac{xy}{2}\\A&=\frac{2.1\times3}{2}\\A&=3.15\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Tall rhombus slanting from upper left to lower right, with the full shorter diagonal and only the lower-right half of the longer diagonal dashed.
spec.mathematics: Full shorter diagonal 10 cm; lower-right half of the other diagonal 12 cm; lower-left side 13 cm. All four sides have matching single equality ticks. The dashed segments meet perpendicularly.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; the full longer diagonal and area belong in the answer.

answer.worked:
The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other.
$$\begin{align*}y&=2\times12\\y&=24\text{ cm}\\A&=\frac{xy}{2}\\A&=\frac{10\times24}{2}\\A&=120\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Right-leaning parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides and a dashed vertical height.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal base 5.5 m; perpendicular height 4 m; right sloping side 5 m. Matching double parallel arrows mark the horizontal sides and matching single arrows mark the sloping sides. A right-angle marker is at the height's foot.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; the area belongs in the answer.

answer.worked:
Use the perpendicular height, $4\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=bh\\A&=5.5\times4\\A&=22\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Rotated parallelogram whose short sides slope up to the right and whose long sides slope down to the right.
spec.mathematics: Lower short side 5.2 m; long left side 9.9 m; dashed perpendicular height 9.8 m from the upper short side to the lower-right vertex. Single parallel arrows mark the short sides and double arrows mark the long sides. A right-angle marker identifies the height at its upper endpoint.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; the area belongs in the answer.

answer.worked:
Use the perpendicular height, $9.8\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=bh\\A&=5.2\times9.8\\A&=50.96\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$
